headline_marked: Controversy over [[PM asks State Minister Ishraque to resign]] amid firearm display
headline: Controversy over PM asks State Minister Ishraque to resign amid firearm display
summary: State Minister Ishraque Hossain denies reports that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman asked him to step down following an anti-drug drive in Gendaria.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain is facing intense scrutiny after videos showed him brandishing a firearm during an 'anti-drug operation' in Gendaria, Dhaka.
Multiple media outlets and state broadcaster BTV reported that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman summoned the minister and asked him to resign due to public outrage over the incident.
However, Ishraque Hossain and his press officer have dismissed these reports as 'completely false' and 'rumours,' stating that no such directive has been issued.
Government sources claim the Prime Minister expressed strong dissatisfaction and reprimanded Ishraque, instructing him to apologize publicly for his conduct.
The incident has caused unease among BNP ministers and lawmakers, who argue that a state minister personally leading an armed operation has embarrassed the government.
Some lawmakers expressed concern that the videos of the minister with a weapon could damage the government's image among foreign diplomats.
In a Facebook post, Ishraque stated that any official instruction from the Prime Minister would be binding and the nation would be informed through a press conference if any decision were taken.
caption:
Did the Prime Minister ask State Minister Ishraque to resign? Conflicting reports emerge after a controversial armed anti-drug drive.

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain is facing intense scrutiny after videos showed him brandishing a firearm during an 'anti-drug operation' in Gendaria, Dhaka.

Multiple media outlets and state broadcaster BTV reported that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman summoned the minister and asked him to resign due to public outrage over the incident.

However, Ishraque Hossain and his press officer have dismissed these reports as 'completely false' and 'rumours,' stating that no such directive has been issued.

Government sources claim the Prime Minister expressed strong dissatisfaction and reprimanded Ishraque, instructing him to apologize publicly for his conduct.

The incident has caused unease among BNP ministers and lawmakers, who argue that a state minister personally leading an armed operation has embarrassed the government.

Some lawmakers expressed concern that the videos of the minister with a weapon could damage the government's image among foreign diplomats.

In a Facebook post, Ishraque stated that any official instruction from the Prime Minister would be binding and the nation would be informed through a press conference if any decision were taken.

Source: The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: 10 killed as [[unauthorised resort fire]] hits Cox's Bazar
headline: 10 killed as unauthorised resort fire hits Cox's Bazar
summary: The TUPTUP Resto & Resort was operating without a fire licence or development approval, despite repeated warnings from authorities.
details: A devastating fire at TUPTUP Resto & Resort in Inani, Cox's Bazar, has killed at least 10 people. Authorities are still working to identify the victims and establish the full death toll.
Investigations reveal the resort was an illegal entity, operating without approval from the deputy commissioner, local union council, or municipal authorities.
The Fire Service and Civil Defence revealed that the resort had been served a written notice in June to apply for a fire licence, but it failed to comply.
The Cox's Bazar Development Authority had issued sequential notices since 2023, including directives to cease operations and demolish the structure because it was built in a no-development zone.
Fire Service officials cited severe staff shortages as a reason for inadequate oversight, stating only one inspector is assigned to monitor 500 to 600 commercial establishments in the district.
Officials estimate that nearly 400 commercial establishments in Cox's Bazar are operating without a valid fire licence, highlighting a systemic failure in safety oversight.
According to the Cox's Bazar Development Authority, many operators disregard the law and continue operating despite repeated warnings and removal orders.
caption:
At least 10 people died in a resort fire in Cox's Bazar. The facility was operating illegally despite repeated warnings from the Fire Service and Development Authority.

A devastating fire at TUPTUP Resto & Resort in Inani, Cox's Bazar, has killed at least 10 people. Authorities are still working to identify the victims and establish the full death toll.

Investigations reveal the resort was an illegal entity, operating without approval from the deputy commissioner, local union council, or municipal authorities.

The Fire Service and Civil Defence revealed that the resort had been served a written notice in June to apply for a fire licence, but it failed to comply.

The Cox's Bazar Development Authority had issued sequential notices since 2023, including directives to cease operations and demolish the structure because it was built in a no-development zone.

Fire Service officials cited severe staff shortages as a reason for inadequate oversight, stating only one inspector is assigned to monitor 500 to 600 commercial establishments in the district.

Officials estimate that nearly 400 commercial establishments in Cox's Bazar are operating without a valid fire licence, highlighting a systemic failure in safety oversight.

According to the Cox's Bazar Development Authority, many operators disregard the law and continue operating despite repeated warnings and removal orders.
